What are exponents and radicals?

An exponent says how many times a base is multiplied by itself: x3=x⋅x⋅x. A radical undoes it: x33=x. The two are the same idea written two ways, because a root is a fractional power, xn=x1/n. A handful of rules let you simplify any product, quotient or power of them.

Try changing the input

Evaluate 16−3/4. The 4 is a fourth root (164=2), the 3 is a cube (23=8) and the minus sign is a reciprocal: 18.

What this calculator does

  • Laws of exponents: simplifies products, quotients and powers of monomials such as (2x3y−2)24x−1y, writing the result with positive exponents.
  • Radicals: simplifies k xaybn by pulling out every perfect nth power.
  • Rational powers: evaluates bp/q exactly or in simplest radical form, with a decimal.

Each result ends with a check: substituting sample values, or raising the answer back to the power of the root.

The ideas behind it

Exponents count factors, so the rules are about counting:

  • Multiplying x3⋅x2 puts 3 + 2 factors together: x5.
  • Dividing cancels factors: x5x2=x3. Carrying on past zero gives negative exponents: x−2=1x2.
  • A power of a power multiplies the counts: (x3)2=x6.

A fractional exponent fits the same rules: (x1/2)2=x1, so x1/2 must be x.

Simplest radical form

A radical is simplified when nothing inside is a perfect nth power: 72=36⋅2=62.

Variables explained

SymbolMeaning

Simplifying a radical, step by step

For k xan:

  1. Split the coefficient k into the largest perfect nth power and what is left.
  2. Divide each exponent a by n: the quotient comes out of the root, the remainder stays in. For example x5 under a square root is x2⋅2+1, so x2 comes out and x stays in.
  3. Multiply the outside parts and the inside parts.

To check, raise the outside part to the power n and multiply by what is inside: it must rebuild the original radicand.

Complete worked example

Problem

Simplify (2x3y−2)24x−1y.

Step 1: Power of a product

(2x3y−2)2=4x6y−4

Step 2: Divide, subtracting exponents

4x6y−44x−1y=x6−(−1) y−4−1=x7y−5

Step 3: Positive exponents

x7y−5=x7y5

Check

With x=1.3 and y=0.7, both the original and x7y5 give about 37.33. ✓

Second worked example: a radical and a rational power

Part 1: Simplify 72x5y2

72=36⋅2,x5=x4⋅x,y2=y2 72x5y2=6x2y2x

Check: (6x2y)2⋅2x=36x4y2⋅2x=72x5y2. ✓

Part 2: Evaluate 16−3/4

16−3/4=1(164)3=123=18=0.125

Practical applications

  • Scientific notation and units: 103×10−6=10−3, converting kilo- and micro- units.
  • Scaling laws: volume grows as length³ and area as length², so a model at scale 110 has 11000 of the volume.
  • Physics formulas: the pendulum period T=2πL/g and Kepler's law T2∝a3.
  • Growth and decay: compound interest and half-lives use powers.

Common mistakes

  1. Multiplying exponents in a product. x3⋅x2=x5, not x6.
  2. Treating a negative exponent as a negative number. 2−3=18, not −8.
  3. Applying a power to only part of a product. (2x)3=8x3, not 2x3.
  4. Splitting a root over a sum. 9+16=5, not 3+4.

Assumptions and limitations

  • Variables are assumed positive, so even roots need no absolute values and division is allowed.
  • The laws mode handles products, quotients and powers of monomials (no sums).
  • Radicands are a single term with an integer coefficient.

Frequently asked questions

What does a fractional exponent mean?

a^(p/q) is the q-th root of a raised to the power p. For example 8^(2/3) = (∛8)² = 4.

How do I simplify a square root?

Write the number as a perfect square times what is left and take the square root of the perfect square: √50 = √(25·2) = 5√2.

Why is any number to the power 0 equal to 1?

Because aⁿ/aⁿ = 1, and by the quotient rule it is also a⁰.

How do I get rid of negative exponents?

Move the factor to the other side of the fraction bar and make the exponent positive: x⁻²y = y/x².
